title: Everest Gave Back A Climber After Seventy-Five Years

segments.narration: Mallory's snow goggles were in his pocket, not his eyes. Everest, and he had been missing for seventy-five years.
Mallory and Sandy Irvine went up on the eighth of June, 1924. Noel Odell watched two dots move on the ridge, then cloud closed.
Conrad Anker found him in 1999 just under twenty-seven thousand feet, a rope still knotted at his waist. Goggles come off when the light goes. So was he coming down from the top?
Probably not. The camera that would prove it was not on him, and neither was the photograph of his wife he meant to leave up there.
In 2024 a glacier far below gave up a boot with Irvine's name tape inside. The camera is still up there.

verdicts.claim: When George Mallory's body was found on Everest his snow goggles were in his pocket rather than over his eyes.
verdicts.note: 79% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article

verdicts.claim: Mallory and Sandy Irvine disappeared high on Everest on 8 June 1924 after Noel Odell's last sighting of them on the ridge.
verdicts.note: 79% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article, including 2 number(s)

verdicts.claim: Conrad Anker found Mallory's body on 1 May 1999 at 26,760 feet, with a rope still tied around his waist that had left crush and rope-jerk marks.
verdicts.note: The expedition article gives 1 May 1999 at about 11:45 a.m., Conrad Anker as the finder, an altitude of 26,760 ft (8,156 m), and a rope at the waist that caused crush injuries and rope-jerk marks.

verdicts.claim: The Vest Pocket Kodak camera was never found on the body, and no photograph of his wife was on him although he had intended to leave one on the summit.
verdicts.note: 71% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article

verdicts.claim: In 2024 a National Geographic team led by Jimmy Chin found a boot and a sock with an A. C. Irvine name tape on the Central Rongbuk Glacier.
verdicts.note: The expedition article and National Geographic's October 2024 announcement both describe a boot, a sock with an 'A. C. Irvine' name tape and a foot found on the Central Rongbuk Glacier by a team led by Jimmy Chin, at least 7,000 ft below Mallory's body, with the cameras still missing.
